### Added

- **Windows Hello, working end to end** (Windows): enabling Hello no longer fails with `create 0x80090027` — the database key is now held through the system KeyCredentialManager surface (direct NGC key creation is fenced to OS components on current Windows), and the Hello prompt comes to the front on its own instead of opening behind the app. The app-lock PIN can remain as the other way in.
- **Text-only mode** (Privacy & security): hide attachments and link previews for unknown senders (default), everyone, or nobody — each hidden item reveals on tap until you trust the chat. Fail-closed: anything it cannot classify counts as unknown.
- **Show in folder** (desktop): the message context menu reveals an attachment's file in the file manager.
- **Relay send failover**: the Relays dialog shows what the last send attempt did, and an optional strict mode keeps sending on the pinned relay only.
- **Invited PWA onboarding**: an invite link walks through account creation and lands with the relay already configured.
- **Roaming hint** (Android): while on data roaming, Velta suggests Text-only mode once per roaming episode — it never switches anything on its own.
- **Linux packages**: .deb, AppImage and Arch (PKGBUILD repackaging the .deb); the bundled core ships as `velta-rpc-server` so it cannot clash with distro `deltachat-rpc-server` packages.

### Fixed

- Privacy & security claimed attachments "stay unencrypted" — they have been encrypted with the database key since #184 (thumbnails and upload staging included). The note now says so; the unencrypted wording remains only for sessions without an OS keychain, where nothing is encrypted.
- Relays: a boot-time crash when the failover log was created before module init.

### Security

- **Attachment encryption at rest is out of preview**: native profiles encrypt blobs, thumbnails and upload staging (VLTA: per-file wrapped keys, seekable 64 KiB chunks). Windows Hello holds the database key through a hardware-backed Hello credential; the app-lock PIN and Windows Hello can each be the key root.
